comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 — that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions — so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists — it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch. See rule G100.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: @typescript-eslint's parser crashes on the native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. @typescript-eslint peer-requires >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, so 6.x is the last usable major. Hold until obsidian-dev-utils migrates.

brace-expansion.why: GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (high, DoS via unbounded expansion) is declared with the single flat range <=5.0.7, which in plain semver also matches the newest 1.x and 2.x releases — so no 1.x/2.x release can ever satisfy it and `npm audit fix` can only offer a downgrade. Every copy must therefore be forced onto >=5.0.8. A bare caret override cannot do that: 5.x exports a namespace (exports.expand), while minimatch 3/5 (`require('brace-expansion')`) and minimatch 8/9 (`__importDefault`) all call the module itself, so they break with `expand is not a function`. The override points at patches/brace-expansion-callable, a wrapper that re-exports the patched 5.x implementation in BOTH shapes (callable default and named .expand, for minimatch 10). The patched implementation is installed under the brace-expansion-upstream alias because the override takes over the real name.
brace-expansion.manualCheck: The check tracks the oldest callable-shape consumer still in the tree. If eslint-plugin-import stops depending on minimatch ^3.x, re-derive whether ANY remaining minimatch major still imports brace-expansion as a callable default (grep node_modules/**/minimatch for `require("brace-expansion")` and `__importDefault`). Once every consumer uses minimatch >=10 (`require("brace-expansion").expand`), the wrapper and the brace-expansion-upstream alias can be dropped for a plain caret override.
